title: ERA5 sea-ice input steps on 1 September 2007 and 1 June 2016 cause local polar winter 2 m temperature steps but change 1979-2024 Arctic-mean warming by less than 1% (NSIDC CDR reference)
abstract: Question: ERA5 changed its sea-ice input on 1 September 2007, from reprocessed OSI SAF (OSI-409-a) to operational OSI SAF (OSI-401-a). How large is the resulting step, and does it bias ERA5 2 m temperature (T2m) and polar warming trends? Approach: we read ERA5 sea-ice concentration (SIC) daily and T2m every third day for 1979-2026 from ARCO-ERA5. We compared SIC with the NOAA/NSIDC CDR v6 on a common 25 km mask and dated steps with the daily NSIDC Sea Ice Index v4. We used the input steps as natural experiments: per 1-degree box, we regressed the T2m change on the artificial ice change, with sector fixed effects, block bootstrap and 37 placebo dates. Results: ERA5 Arctic extent fell 0.26 million km2 in one day on 2007-09-01 and rose 0.50 million km2 in one day on 2016-06-01 (an undocumented step); the Sea Ice Index has no such changes. A blind search puts the largest ERA5-minus-CDR Arctic extent break at 2007-09-01. The 2007 Arctic area step is -0.24 million km2 (95% CI -0.29 to -0.18), mostly in marginal seas in winter. Thus ERA5 shows 72% less Arctic ice-area loss than the CDR in 2007-2024 and 89% less in 2010-2025, but the same loss over 1979-2024. ERA5 T2m responds by -9.0 K per unit ice fraction in Arctic winter (95% CI -11.6 to -6.6; -9.3 and -8.8 for the two events separately; placebo SD 0.55), near 0 in summer, and -20.3 K in Antarctic winter. Because the ice errors are local, the 66.5-90N mean T2m bias is only +0.019 K in 2007-2016; the 1979-2024 Arctic trend (0.692 K per decade) and amplification ratio (3.36) change by less than 1%. Regional 2007-2024 winter trends are too low by 0.07-0.10 K per decade in several marginal seas, and the 60-90S 1979-2024 trend is 13-22% too low. Limitations: the CDR is an imperfect reference and only changes of ERA5-minus-CDR are used; the 1987 sensor-change step cannot be assigned; there is no comparison north of 84.5N; the response is a local estimate (coarser fixed effects give 0-30% larger values); no independent over-ice air temperatures exist for 2007.

Consequences: zonal-mean T2m bias, ERA5 and CDR Arctic ice area trends, and winter T2m trend errors by region.
